name: Chakato
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog entry retired/archival; no grammar, phonology, or sketch located

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages chak1275 (Chakato, retired bookkeeping) and jort1240 (Jakattoe [jrt]) with reference list (10 refs).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; lists Blench & Bulkaam 2019 (wordlist), Decker et al. 2020 (socling/wordlist), Blench 2016 CALL slides, Hoffmann 1975 comparative phonology of Angas-Goemai, plus overviews.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Adedamola Aregbesola, Fittokka Gobak, John Muniru, John Sacson, Christina Riepe & Samuel Eju. 2020. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Jakattoe [jrt] Language of Plateau State, Nigeria, with Reference to Jorto. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2020-011. Dallas: SIL International. 55 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.2 Phonology (pp. 11-13) gives tentative consonant and vowel inventories compared against Blench 2019; Appendix E states 'The transcriptions are preliminary since no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features was conducted.' No stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2020. Change Request 2020-007: adopted update [jrt] (2021-01-15) -- reference name Jorto -> Jakattoe.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; identity document only (Chakato/Jakato/Jakattoe spellings, autonym [dʒækɜ́to], Jorto is an exonym).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Michael Bulkaam. 2019. Jakato, an undocumented language of Central Nigeria. Circulation draft, Jos, 19 October 2019. i+19 pp. Kay Williamson Educational Foundation (rogerblench.info; downloaded from the Internet Archive).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 3-5) covers vowels, consonants (plain/palatalised/labialised) and 3.3 Tones (p. 4): 'Like the other A3 languages, Jakato has three phonetic tones, marked Low, Mid and High.. This suggests it is underlyingly a two-tone language'. No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the paper.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Current research on the A3 West Chadic languages. In Henry Tourneux & Yvonne Treis (eds.), Selected papers from the VIIIth Biennial International Colloquium on the Chadic Languages, 1-27. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Group-wide overview of A3 (Central West Chadic) phonology that both the Jakato sketch and the SIL survey rely on for prosodic generalisations; the most likely place for any remark on stress vs. tone in Jakato and its Pan-cluster relatives.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2016. Five unexpected Chadic languages and the sorry tale of Jorto. Paper presented at the Colloquium on African Languages and Linguistics (CALL), Leiden, September 2016. 29 pp.
